prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal]
Recreate Hokusai's Great Wave as a single-file low-poly 3D wallpaper and record the print's boats and mountain.

[action]
Built ./scene/index.html with Three.js from the allowed CDN: curling great wave with foam claws, right wave, Mount Fuji, three rowing boats, sea bands, procedural clouds and spray, all with gentle motion. Wrote ./result.json. Opened the file in a browser, verified the render across three checks, and closed the tab I opened.

[result]
Delivered ./scene/index.html and ./result.json. Browser render confirmed the composition, palette and subjects. result.json: {"boats": 3, "mountain": "Mount Fuji"}.

[next]
Nothing pending. Found: three boats and Mount Fuji. I know because I inspected ./print.jpg visually: three distinct rowing boats appear (left trough, mid-right, foreground), and the small snow-capped cone in the central trough is Fuji, confirmed by the title cartouche 神奈川沖浪裏 from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
